name: rock-base
concept: A slow, small rotation from the bottom, like an object that rocks on a flat base. Use it for a toy, bottle, or icon that stands upright.

name: rock-corner-left
concept: A slow rotation pivoting from the bottom-left corner, as if the element is pinned there. Use it for a flag, tag, or banner anchored at one point.

name: rock-corner-right
concept: A slow rotation pivoting from the bottom-right corner, mirroring a left-pinned sway. Use it for a flag or tag anchored at its right edge.

name: rock-deep
concept: A slower, wider rotation from the bottom than a standard base rock. Use it for a heavier object that settles into a long, deep rocking motion.

name: nudge-up
concept: A small, continuous upward shift and return. Use it to point attention at something above the element, like an onboarding hint pointing up.

name: nudge-down
concept: A small, continuous downward shift and return. Use it to point attention at something below the element, like a hint toward a lower panel.

name: nudge-vertical
concept: A small, continuous up-and-down shift, centered on the element. Use it for a vertical attention cue when direction does not matter.

name: nudge-double
concept: Two small upward bumps followed by a pause, then the cycle repeats. Use it for a more insistent hint than a single nudge, without feeling urgent.

name: drift-ne
concept: A very slow, small diagonal wander toward the top-right corner and back. Use it for a background element that seems to drift lazily.

name: drift-nw
concept: A very slow, small diagonal wander toward the top-left corner and back. Use it for a background element that seems to drift lazily.

name: drift-se
concept: A very slow, small diagonal wander toward the bottom-right corner and back. Use it for a background element that seems to drift lazily.

name: drift-sw
concept: A very slow, small diagonal wander toward the bottom-left corner and back. Use it for a background element that seems to drift lazily.

name: drift-haze
concept: A very slow diagonal drift paired with a soft dip in opacity at its farthest point. Use it for an element that seems to drift through haze.

name: meander
concept: A small, irregular wander that loops through several small stops instead of a simple back-and-forth. Use it for an element that feels aimless and unhurried.

name: meander-wide
concept: A looser, larger version of a gentle wander, moving through six small stops. Use it when the wander needs more visible reach without losing its calm.

name: meander-horizontal
concept: An irregular wander biased along the horizontal axis, with only a slight vertical drift. Use it for a wide element where horizontal motion reads better.

name: meander-vertical
concept: An irregular wander biased along the vertical axis, like a slow, drunken walk upward and downward. Use it for a tall element where vertical drift reads better.

name: meander-pause
concept: An irregular wander that lingers at each stop before moving on, giving it a choppier rhythm than a smooth meander. Use it for a more deliberate, hesitant drift.

name: pendulum-wide
concept: A slow, wide rotation from the top, wider than a standard gentle sway. Use it for a hanging element that needs a more visible, pendulum-like swing.

name: pendulum-slow
concept: An even slower, wider rotation from the top than a standard pendulum swing. Use it for a large hanging element with a long, heavy swing.

name: pendulum-corner
concept: A slow rotation pivoting from the top-left corner instead of the top center. Use it for an element hinged at one edge, like a corner-mounted sign.

name: pendulum-drift-bob
concept: A wide pendulum swing combined with a small vertical bob at its outer point. Use it for a hanging element that feels weighted, like a heavy pendant.

name: loll-left
concept: A slow lean to the left that holds briefly before returning, like a head tilting and resting. Use it for a relaxed, idle attention cue.

name: loll-right
concept: A slow lean to the right that holds briefly before returning, like a head tilting and resting. Use it for a relaxed, idle attention cue.

name: loll-bob
concept: A slow lean combined with a small downward dip that holds briefly before returning. Use it for a drowsy, relaxed idle motion.

name: loll-deep
concept: A deeper lean that holds for longer than a standard loll before returning. Use it for a heavier or more exaggerated drowsy idle motion.

name: skew-sway
concept: A slow, continuous skew oscillation instead of a rotation. Use it for a different visual quality of sway, like a soft rubbery wobble.

name: skew-sway-wide
concept: A wider skew oscillation than a standard skew sway, for more visible shear. Use it for an element that needs a more pronounced soft wobble.

name: skew-tilt
concept: A slow, continuous vertical skew oscillation, shearing the element top to bottom instead of side to side. Use it for a distinct wobble on a tall element.

name: skew-drift
concept: A skew oscillation combined with a small horizontal shift. Use it for an element that seems to wobble while gently sliding side to side.

name: skew-breathe
concept: A skew oscillation paired with a slight dip in opacity. Use it for an ambient element that wobbles softly while it fades in and out.

name: nudge-corner-ne
concept: A small, quick diagonal shift toward the top-right corner and back. Use it to point attention toward something in that corner, like a badge or menu.

name: nudge-corner-nw
concept: A small, quick diagonal shift toward the top-left corner and back. Use it to point attention toward something in that corner, like a badge or menu.

name: nudge-corner-se
concept: A small, quick diagonal shift toward the bottom-right corner and back. Use it to point attention toward something in that corner, like a badge or menu.

name: nudge-corner-sw
concept: A small, quick diagonal shift toward the bottom-left corner and back. Use it to point attention toward something in that corner, like a badge or menu.

name: orbit-drift-loop
concept: A slow, small circular wander that loops the element around its resting point. Use it for an ambient element that feels like it is gently orbiting.

name: orbit-loop-tight
concept: A smaller, quicker version of a circular wander. Use it for an element that needs a subtle orbiting motion without much visible reach.

name: orbit-tilt
concept: A circular wander combined with a small rotation, like a leaf turning as it drifts. Use it for a more organic, tumbling ambient motion.

name: orbit-reverse
concept: A circular wander that loops in the opposite direction from a standard orbit drift. Use it to vary the direction of motion across several elements.

name: lean-corner-ne
phrase: lean and shift toward a corner
concept: A rotation and small shift toward the top-right corner that holds briefly before returning. Use it to draw the eye toward content in that corner.

name: lean-corner-sw
phrase: lean and shift toward the opposite corner
concept: A rotation and small shift toward the bottom-left corner that holds briefly before returning. Use it to draw the eye toward content in that corner.

name: tilt-drift
concept: A slow, combined rotation and diagonal wander, back and forth without holding. Use it for an ambient element that feels like it is gently tumbling as it drifts.

name: tilt-drift-reverse
phrase: drift while tilting the other way
concept: The same combined rotation and diagonal wander as a tilting drift, but leaning the opposite way. Use it to vary the motion across a set of elements.

name: bob-tilt
concept: A small vertical bob combined with a slight rotation, pivoting from the top. Use it for an element that feels like it bobs and tilts at once.

name: bob-tilt-wide
concept: A wider, slower version of a bob-and-tilt motion. Use it for an element that needs a more visible combined bounce and lean.

name: bob-lean
concept: A vertical dip combined with a lean that holds briefly before returning. Use it for a drowsy, weighted idle motion, like a heavy head nodding and settling.

name: sway-asymmetric
concept: A rotation that swings between two sides, holding one side longer than the other. Use it for a sway with a less mechanical, more natural rhythm.

name: arc-nudge
concept: A small, quick shift that traces a short curved path instead of a straight line. Use it for a more playful attention cue than a straight nudge.

name: wander-drift
concept: A very slow, irregular two-axis wander with a wider reach than a standard meander. Use it for a background element that drifts on a long, lazy cycle.

name: sway-deep-bottom
concept: A wide rotation from the bottom that holds briefly on one side before returning. Use it for a standing element with a heavier, more deliberate rock.
